text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.92% today after rising sharply over the past two weeks, giving back some gains as oil prices pulled back slightly. Brent crude dropped below $110 after hitting $126.55 globally earlier in the week, driven by escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East — Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and Iran's threats of retaliation had pushed prices higher, but the intensity of those concerns appears to have eased today.

The refining backdrop remains supportive: refineries are running at 93.5% capacity and oil storage is moderate at 698.56 million barrels, which typically favors refiner margins when crude is elevated. However, the two-week rally (up 9.28%) was built largely on geopolitical risk premiums, and pullbacks in that risk tend to pressure refiner stocks as much as they do crude futures.
